stem: Prakash walks from his office O to his home H along the following route: 16 km East, then 4 km North, then 9 km South, then 4 km West. A bird flies directly in a straight line from H back to O. What is the direction of the bird's flight and its distance?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Net displacement O to H: EW=16-4=12E, NS=4-9=-5S. H is 12E and 5S of O. The bird flies H to O: direction is North-West (opposite of SE). Distance=sqrt(12^2+5^2)=sqrt(169)=13 km.
South-East is the direction from O to H, not from H to O; the query asks for the return direction, which is the reverse.
21 km arises as 12+9 or similar: results from adding displacements without proper cancellation, giving 12+9=21 instead of sqrt(12^2+5^2)=13.

sqrt(119) = sqrt(100+19) arises from a slip: using 10^2+something or (16-4-9)^2 + (4-4)^2 = 9^2 = 81? Re-route: using net NS as 4 instead of |4-9|=5, giving sqrt(12^2+4^2)=sqrt(160). Alternatively sqrt(119)=sqrt((12-1)^2+(5-1)^2) which is a slip subtracting 1 from each component.

explanation: Step 1 - compute net displacement from O to H. Resolve each axis independently. EW: +16-4=+12 (East). NS: +4-9=-5 (South). H is 12 km East and 5 km South of O. Step 2 - the bird flies from H to O, which is the reverse direction: North-West. Step 3 - straight-line distance: sqrt(12^2+5^2)=sqrt(144+25)=sqrt(169)=13 km. Recognise the 5-12-13 Pythagorean triple.

explanation_sections.punchline: Resolve the route to net (12E, 5S); the return leg is North-West and the 5-12-13 triple gives 13 km.
explanation_sections.approach: Deductive trace: (1) Cancel opposite-direction legs on each axis: EW: 16E-4W=12E; NS: 4N-9S=5S. (2) H is at coordinates (12,-5) from O. (3) The reversed query: direction from H to O is opposite to O-to-H direction. O-to-H is South-East, so H-to-O is North-West. (4) Distance = sqrt(12^2+5^2) = 13 km (5-12-13 triple).
explanation_sections.lesson: A reversed-query problem has two hidden steps: compute net displacement, then reverse its direction. The distance is always the same regardless of direction of travel.
explanation_sections.timing: 90-120 seconds. Three traps: (a) forgetting to reverse the direction (gives SE, option 2); (b) adding path lengths instead of net displacements (gives 21 km, option 3); (c) arithmetic slip in Pythagoras (option 4). Spotting 5-12-13 after resolving axes saves time.
